###### How it works

## BugSplat is crash and error reporting for teams serious about stability and performance.

Your app will break. Whether you find and fix it quickly is up to you. BugSplat makes a fast, quality response part of your workflow: capture, diagnose, ship, and confirm the fix worked. All in one tool.

### It shows up. Immediately.

Crashes, exceptions, errors, and user-reported issues captured across every platform. Symbols resolved automatically, stack traces readable from the start. You see it on your dashboard, not as an angry email, or worse, never.

### The noise sorts itself out.

Ten thousand crash reports might be twelve distinct problems. BugSplat groups them by stack signature, skipping OS and runtime noise out of the box. See what's actually happening, weigh it, decide what to fix first.

### You see exactly why it broke.

Symbolicated stack traces with readable function names land you on the exact line that broke. Exception code, message, platform, and environment in one view. No debugger required.

### You fix it and prove it worked.

You know exactly what broke and where. No reproducing locally, no guessing. Tag the release, reprocess against new symbols, and BugSplat tells you whether crash rates actually dropped.

### It doesn't happen again.

Alerts when crash rates spike. Daily and weekly digests, version-over-version trend analysis, and regression detection so nothing that comes back gets buried.

BugSplat started as a side project in 2005 with one goal: make it easier to find and fix bugs in production software. Since then we've helped a lot of people keep their users happier, spend more time building their app instead of supporting it, and ship code with more confidence.

We're a [small bootstrapped company](https://www.bugsplat.com/about/). What that means is our success comes from one place: you liking what we make. We don't have growth targets dictated by VCs or a board pressuring us to add features. Our only goals are to make great reporting tools and build a company we're proud to work at.

Take a look around. If you have questions, reach out. You'll hear back from someone who works on the product every day and has been here for close to a decade. If our tools look interesting, please consider [trying them in your next project](https://app.bugsplat.com/v2/sign-up).

-The BugSplat Team

# Features

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/features

# Get crashes under control before they get out of hand

BugSplat captures, symbolicates, and groups crashes, errors, and other issues automatically so your team spends time fixing problems, not tracking them down.

No credit card · SOC 2 Type II · GDPR compliant · 14-day full access trial

###### The problem

## Most crash tools make debugging harder than it needs to be.

Crashes scatter across tools. Stack traces need manual symbolication. You're not sure which issue to fix first, or whether last week's fix actually held. It adds up to a lot of time not fixing things. BugSplat is built to remove that overhead.

[   ](https://www.bugsplat.com/features/crash-reporting/)

### Crash reporting

Smart grouping, deep context, and readable stack traces give you answers without noise or guesswork.

Explore crash reporting →[   ](https://www.bugsplat.com/features/error-reporting/)

### Error monitoring

Capture handled exceptions and non-fatal errors so issues don't disappear just because the software kept running.

Explore error reporting →[   ](https://www.bugsplat.com/features/stability-monitoring/)

### Release & stability monitoring

Track crashes and errors across versions, platforms, and environments to spot regressions early and ship with confidence.

Explore stability monitoring →###### Capture

### If it broke, it's in your dashboard.

Crashes, handled exceptions, silent failures behind retries. BugSplat captures all of it automatically, with no extra instrumentation. The issues that usually disappear into support tickets show up here instead.

Detect crashes hidden behind retries or recoveries

Reduce support tickets before they happen

No extra instrumentation or dashboards to manage

###### Context

### One crash report. Everything you need to debug it.

Full call stack, thread state, memory, OS, GPU, build version, and user impact. In one view. You don't need four other tools open to understand what happened.

Full call stacks, threads, memory state, and system details

Readable symbolication with real function names and line numbers

Real crash data from real users, not reproductions

###### Prioritization

### Fix the crash that matters most, not the one that arrived last.

Volume-weighted grouping puts the issues affecting the most users at the top. 10,000 reports might be 12 unique problems. BugSplat shows you the 12.

Know your real crash rate instead of estimating

Prioritize by impact, not just volume

One clear view, not a maze of filters

BugSplat isn't just a service provider. They're a true partner in our success.

Jason Antonacci

DevOps Engineer, SketchUp

###### Stability

### Closing a ticket isn't the same as fixing a crash.

BugSplat tracks stability across every release. Regressions are flagged automatically. You know whether last Tuesday's deploy actually helped, without going looking for it.

Track stability across versions and releases

Spot patterns before they become systemic

Measure progress, not just activity

###### What's new

## Always shipping. Here's what's fresh.

We build in the open and ship often. These are the newest additions to BugSplat, each one driven by real requests from teams using the product.

New Feature

### User Feedback

Not every issue crashes the app. Users hit bugs that frustrate them: broken flows, visual glitches, unexpected behavior. But the software keeps running. Those issues used to disappear into support tickets or, worse, go unreported entirely.

BugSplat's user feedback capture lets you collect bug reports directly from your app. Each submission lands in the same dashboard as your crash data, with the user's description, IP address, email, and any custom attributes you attach: OS, build number, environment, feature flags, locale, plan, team, region, priority, and more.

Attachments come along too. One place for everything that's going wrong, whether or not it throws an exception.

New Feature

### Version Comparison

Shipping a fix without knowing if it worked is guesswork. Version comparison gives you a side-by-side view of crash rates across releases so you can see at a glance whether v2.4.1 is actually more stable than v2.4.0, or if you just introduced three new problems.

Choose a custom timeframe to see which versions accounted for what percentage of your crashes. Use the charting tool to tell the difference between a trend and a spike. Then bring that data to standups, sprint reviews, or release sign-offs so "are we getting better?" has an actual answer.

New Feature

### BugSplat for your AI assistant

Stop alt-tabbing between your IDE and a crash dashboard. The BugSplat MCP server lets Cursor, Claude Desktop, and other MCP-compatible tools pull your crashes, stack traces, attachments, and even file defects, all from the editor.

It's an early experiment, not a polished product. Bobby wrote up where it stands and where we're taking it next.

## Everything you need to debug. Nothing you don't.

Clear crash data, a UI built for debugging, and workflows that scale to your team.

### Capture everything clearly

#### Simple symbolication

Clean stack traces with real function names and line numbers. Upload symbols once or sync directly from S3 and external stores.

#### Full crash dumps

Go deeper when you need to. Capture full memory dumps for the bugs that refuse to explain themselves.

#### Rich visual context

See what users saw. Attach screenshots or video to understand crashes without guesswork.

#### Custom file attachments

Logs, configs, and diagnostics live right on the crash report. Preview files instantly, no downloads required.

### Understand what's actually happening

#### Smart crash grouping

Duplicates handled automatically. Focus on unique crashes, not endless copies of the same stack trace.

#### Smarter crash grouping

Tell BugSplat which stack frames matter and which to ignore. Crashes get grouped by the function, module, or file you actually care about, so OS and runtime noise stops drowning out the real bugs.

#### Custom attributes

Attach the data that matters. GPU state, user actions, feature flags, or anything else. Fully searchable, zero friction.

### Find patterns and measure progress

#### Search, filter, and query

Build queries across any field: version, user, IP, stack function, custom attributes your SDK uploads, or date ranges. Filter and group results in the dashboard, share links with your team, or hit the API directly.

#### Flexible group by

Slice crash data by OS, version, hardware, or custom fields to uncover patterns hiding in plain sight.

#### Version comparison

Compare releases to see if stability is improving. Understand what's new, what's fixed, and what's regressing over time.

#### Smart regression detection

Know when a fixed bug comes back. See exactly what percentage of a release is new crashes, regressions, or previously fixed issues.

### See what matters now

#### Stability dashboard

Crash rate, top issues, regression status, and version health. One view, no digging.

#### Release-over-release charting

Compare releases and track crashes over time. See stability trends, top issues in a version, and how new crashes compare to regressions.

### Act automatically

#### Automatic issue creation

Create tickets when new crashes appear, volumes spike, or regressions return. Fully customizable and predictable.

#### Bi-directional issue tracking

Crash reports and Jira tickets stay in sync. Update once, reflected everywhere.

#### Talk directly with your users

Use our Custom Support Response to guide users to updates or fixes the moment they hit a known issue. No manual follow-up required.

### Collaborate and stay organized

#### Crash metadata & annotations

Attach anything that adds context. Add notes, custom metadata, or API-driven annotations directly to crash reports so important details never get lost.

#### Crash assignment & status

Assign crashes, discuss fixes, and track status directly on the report. Keep ownership, progress, and decisions visible without bouncing between tools.

### Built for real-world use

#### Serious about security

SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant. Modern security practices, no shortcuts.

#### Dark mode

Light, dark, or system-synced. Easy on the eyes during long debugging sessions.

###### Crash reporting

# From crash to clarity. Fast.

Trusted by great companies to splat their bugs

###### Crash reporting

## One system for every platform.

Desktop, mobile, web, consoles, and game engines. One place. No stitching together platform-specific tools.

### Cross-platform capture

One SDK per platform. All crash data flows into one consistent dashboard.

[Platform docs](https://docs.bugsplat.com/introduction/getting-started/integrations)

### Root-cause grouping

Crashes are grouped automatically. Regressions and root causes stand out.

[How grouping works](https://docs.bugsplat.com/introduction/development/grouping-crashes)

### Clear grouping, less guesswork

Symbolicated stack traces grouped around real failure points. Compare versions, track regressions, and see impact at a glance.

### One dashboard, all your crashes

Unreal, Unity, C++, .NET, Electron, mobile, consoles. It all lands in a single, consistent view. One login. One source of truth.

### Reliable under load, transparent under pressure

Launch days, bad patches, sudden spikes: crash capture stays automatic. Storage, retention, and scaling are clear. No guesswork when it matters most.

### And plugs that data straight into your workflow

Push crashes into Jira, GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps. Notify Slack or Teams. Use the API to shape the data your way.

###### Error reporting

## Stability first, not observability sprawl.

You don't need another platform to manage. You need to know what's breaking for users.

### Fatal and non-fatal in one view

Crashes and handled errors in one dashboard. One stability picture.

[Crash reporting](https://www.bugsplat.com/features/crash-reporting/)

### Consistent across every platform

Errors are captured and grouped the same way everywhere you ship.

[Platform docs](https://docs.bugsplat.com/introduction/getting-started/integrations)

### Capture handled and unhandled errors

Track exceptions whether they crash the app or not. If something throws or enters an unexpected state, you see it with full context.

### Group errors around real causes

Grouped by root cause so patterns emerge fast. See when a release introduces regressions and prioritize by real user impact.

### Add context that makes issues reproducible

Attach custom attributes, feature flags, build versions, and environment data. Enough signal to reproduce and fix.

### Route errors to the tools you already use

Create issues in Jira, GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps, manually from a crash report or automatically with rules. Notify Slack or Teams. Use the API however you need.

# Stability Monitoring

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/features/stability-monitoring

###### Stability monitoring

# Ship with confidence.

Track crashes and errors across every version, environment, and platform. Spot a bad release the moment it ships, before users start complaining and support tickets pile up.

Trusted by great companies to splat their bugs

###### Stability monitoring

## Know the direction of your product stability.

A single crash count is just a snapshot. Stability is the trend behind it. BugSplat gives you the long view, so you can tell a one-off blip from a real regression and act on what matters.

### See regressions immediately

Compare versions side by side. Did the release help or hurt?

[Crash reporting](https://www.bugsplat.com/features/crash-reporting/)

### Track trends, not just spikes

Monitor crash and error rates over time. See the direction, not just the spikes.

[How grouping works](https://docs.bugsplat.com/introduction/development/grouping-crashes)

### Compare versions with clarity

View crash rates for one version next to another. Spot regressions without digging through raw reports.

### Monitor stability over time

Track trends across days, weeks, and releases. Is stability improving, flat, or getting worse?

### Break down stability by environment

Filter by environment, platform, or release channel. Spot issues before they spread.

### Regressions show up here, not in your support queue

Version-by-version tracking flags new crash patterns the moment a release goes out. You see it before your users report it.

# Custom Support Response

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/features/custom-support-response

# Custom Support Responses

BugSplat's **Custom Support Responses** let you communicate
          directly with your users the moment a crash happens. Instead of digging
          through forums or DMing support, they see a clean, branded message from
          your team: what happened, what to do next, and when it'll be fixed. Instant
          peace of mind.

## Why it matters

- **Keep players in the loop**: Let users know you're already on the case, or give them a quick fix so they can jump back in.
- **Reduce support tickets**: When users get answers in real time, they stop flooding Discord, forums, and email with the same report.
- **Look pro**: A sleek, branded message in your crash dialog sends the signal that your team knows what it's doing, even when things go wrong.

## How it works

Custom Support Responses are tied to crash groups, which BugSplat
          organizes using [grouping rules](https://docs.bugsplat.com/introduction/development/grouping-crashes#auto-group-rules). That way, when a specific crash type hits, users see a specific message tailored to that issue.

You can define fallback messages for all crashes, or target them by localization, platform, or any attribute you choose. Want to show a different message to German users running version 1.1.4? No problem.

And yes, markdown is fully supported. Toss in links, code blocks, whatever your support team needs to get the point across.

## No extra portals. No added steps.

You configure and preview responses right inside your BugSplat dashboard. No extra tools, no uploading HTML, no weird configs. Just click, write, and go.

## Want to see it in action?

Check out our full implementation guide and code walkthrough in [this blog post](https://blog.bugsplat.com/bringing-custom-crash-responses-to-unreal-engine/). It's got everything you need to get up and running fast.

---

# How It Works

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/how-it-works

###### How it works

# When something breaks, you shouldn't have to become a detective.

Capture every crash. Group by root cause. Ship the fix. Five steps, and you know your software is stable.

No credit card · 14-day trial

## Something breaks. You know immediately.

Most teams find out about crashes one of two ways: a user complains, or someone happens to check a log. Both are too late.

BugSplat captures crashes the moment they happen. Full stack traces, thread state, memory context, environment details. Desktop apps, mobile, web, game consoles. It all shows up in one dashboard.

No manual log parsing. No "can you try to reproduce that?" No waiting for angry emails.

- Crashes surface immediately, no waiting for user reports
- Symbols resolved automatically from the start
- Desktop, mobile, web, consoles: one source of truth

## Ten thousand crashes. Twelve actual problems.

Raw crash counts are noise. Your inbox fills with reports, and they all look urgent. They're not.

BugSplat groups related crashes by root cause automatically, then sorts by user impact. That "critical" crash hitting 3 users? It goes below the one quietly affecting 2,000.

You see what matters first. Not what's loudest.

- 10,000 reports might be 12 unique issues. Grouping shows you the 12
- Sort by user impact, not noise
- Automatic de-duplication across versions and platforms

## From stack trace to "oh, I see it."

Symbolicated function names. Line numbers. Thread state. OS version, GPU, build number, user actions leading up to the crash.

Everything you need to understand the problem without reproducing it. Because recreating a crash that only happens on AMD GPUs running Windows 11 with a specific driver version... that's not debugging. That's archaeology.

BugSplat gives you the context to skip straight to the fix.

- Readable function names and line numbers, not memory addresses
- OS, GPU, build version, user actions: full context in one view
- Grouped by root cause so you fix the problem, not the symptom

## Ship it. Then prove it worked.

Fix the bug. Push the release. BugSplat shows you if the crash rate dropped.

If it didn't, or if something new cropped up, you'll know before your users do. Regression detection isn't a premium add-on. It's how crash reporting should work.

Every release should be more stable than the last. Now you can prove it.

- Stability trends across releases, not just raw counts
- Regressions flagged before they reach more users
- Know when it's safe to ship

## Stay ahead of the next one.

You fixed the crash. Great. But software doesn't stop breaking.

Alerts hit Slack, Discord, or Teams the moment something spikes. Daily and weekly digests land in your inbox with the highlights. Version-over-version analytics show whether things are getting better or worse.

This isn't about watching dashboards all day. It's about knowing, without checking, that your software is stable. And when it isn't, knowing exactly where to look.

- Alerts to Slack, Discord, Teams, or email when crash rates spike
- Daily and weekly reports with the highlights that matter
- Version analysis: historical trends, release-over-release comparison
- Regression analysis: automatically flags issues that appeared in previous versions so you prioritize bugs that keep coming back
- Know if you're getting better or worse, version to version

### That's the whole thing.

No forty-page setup guide. No month-long integration project. Add a few lines of code. See your crashes. Fix them. Ship better software.

###### Why BugSplat

## Why teams rely on BugSplat

#### Predictable pricing

No usage-based surprises. Clear limits and straightforward upgrades. Your bill doesn't spike with your crash volume.

#### Real support, from engineers

When something breaks, you talk to the people who built it. Not a queue. Not a maze. The team you reach understands crash workflows firsthand.

#### 20 years of experience

Bootstrapped and independent since 2005. We're building for stability, not an exit. If it's not right, we make it right.

#### Secure by default

SOC 2 Type II audited and GDPR compliant. SSO, MFA, per-database access, and PII obfuscation built in.

#### 99.99% uptime

It holds up during launch week, not just quiet Tuesdays. Crash reporting that's there when it matters most.

#### Teams that stay organized

Add and remove users in seconds. Set clear roles. Manage access across teams without spreadsheets or guesswork.

###### FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

BugSplat is focused on crash and error reporting, not broad monitoring. That means deeper crash data, predictable limits, and workflows built for debugging real failures. When things get complicated, you talk to engineers who understand crash pipelines.

Yes. Teams regularly move from other platforms or homegrown systems. We help you plan the transition so symbols, grouping, and version tracking work correctly from day one.

# What we're working on

We don't keep a fancy public roadmap full of vague promises. We're a small, bootstrapped team, so we stay fast, focused, and fiercely customer-driven. If something matters to the folks using BugSplat, we prioritize it. That's our roadmap. Simple as that.

Got an idea or noticed something missing? [Shoot us an email](mailto:support@bugsplat.com?subject=BugSplat%20Feature%20Request), drop a note on [Discord](https://discord.gg/K4KjjRV5ve), or [grab coffee with us in Denver or Boulder](https://calendly.com/bugsplat/in-person-coffee-with-joey-bugsplat-clone). We read every message, and what you share directly shapes what we
          build.

### Currently in the works

-  **AI, tooling, and access**: Better AI integrations, MCP improvements, a new CLI, and improved authentication with granular permissions.
-  **Deeper App Health Metrics**: Application starts, uptime stats, and extending ANR and Hang Detection to new platforms, plus more signals for performance and user success beyond crashes.
-  **Org-level Admin Role**: Easier management of multiple teams and organization-wide settings for larger companies and studios.

Curious what's already shipped? Head over to the [changelog](https://changelog.bugsplat.com/).

# About

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/about

###### About BugSplat

# Helping teams find and fix bugs since 2005.

Since Dave started BugSplat as a side project over twenty years ago we've been working hard to build the best tools for finding and fixing crashes, errors, and other defects.

Today we're still independent, still bootstrapped, and still small enough that when you reach out, you talk to the people who actually build and run BugSplat.

2005

Started as a side project

100%

Bootstrapped and independent

Billion+

Crashes and errors processed

Millions

Installed games and apps supported

The story so far

BugSplat started in 2005 as a side project by Dave and a couple of colleagues from a large CAD company. That job gave them firsthand experience building a custom crash reporter from scratch. The experience pointed to three things:

- Crash reporting is a nearly magical tool for finding and fixing defects.
- Software gets more stable when developers have good crash data. Everyone should have access to it.
- Building and maintaining a crash reporter is a lot of work.

At the time, there was no self-service crash reporting tool on the market. If you wanted crash data, you built the infrastructure yourself. Large companies could staff a dedicated team for that. Everyone else was out of luck.

That gap is what BugSplat was built to close.

Nights and weekends went into development. In 2005, BugSplat launched with SketchUp as its first customer, with Dave running the code and the servers himself.

The next chapter came in the mid-2010s. The project had found real traction in game development, and Joey and Bobby joined to help turn a side project into a full business. Since then the focus has stayed the same: build a tool developers actually rely on, for apps and games of all sizes.

Twenty years in, the priorities haven't changed: crash data you can actually use, a UI that stays out of your way, and real people on the other end when you need help.

We're still 100% bootstrapped and independent. That means we answer only to our customers. No investors pulling the roadmap in a different direction. We build what the people using BugSplat actually need.

If you're already a BugSplat user, thank you. If you're not, we'd love to show you what we've built.

Cheers,

-The BugSplat Team

“The BugSplat team is SUPER responsive and helpful whenever we reach out.”

Karl Schmidt

Technical Director, Gasket Games


“BugSplat's impact on our product quality and customer satisfaction is remarkable. Their technical expertise and responsiveness make them a truly valued development partner.”

Jason Antonacci

Senior DevOps Engineer, SketchUp


How we work

## What we believe

### Your subscription funds the next feature

We're bootstrapped, which means our customers are the only reason BugSplat exists and improves. Everyone on the team handles support. That's not a policy, it's the reality of building something you're actually responsible for. When you reach out, you get someone who understands what they're talking about and has a stake in the outcome.

### Small teams do more than you think

Being a small team means each person covers a wide range of responsibilities. That breadth, across engineering, support, product, and infrastructure, leads to better decisions and fewer handoff failures. People who understand the whole system build better parts of it.

### Every task is bigger than it looks

How often has a "small" task taken three times as long as expected? Always. That's why we do less, better. We're not trying to out-feature anyone. We build straightforward, useful, and reliable tools. Not overly complicated ones.

### We've been remote since day one

BugSplat has headquarters in Boulder, CO, where we onboard team members and hold all-hands. But our team is fully remote and always has been. One of the best things about working in software is the freedom it can give people. We try to maximize that.

### We give back

BugSplat is a member of the Pledge 1% initiative, committing 1% of profits to causes we care about. Right now that includes Stripe's Carbon Capture program. We're especially interested in organizations working on sustainability, inclusion, and building a better tech industry.

The team

# Game Development

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/for/game-development

# Fix crashes before your players find them

BugSplat catches, groups, and prioritizes crashes across every platform you ship on - so your team always knows what broke, what matters, and what to fix first.

Trusted by studios shipping great games

###### The problem

## You can't test what players will actually do

Different hardware, drivers, engines, and platforms, and players who ignore your test plan. When a crash slips through, you find out in reviews, not in QA.

#### Too Many Combinations to Test

Crashes show up on hardware your test machines never saw. By the time players report them, reviews are already written.

#### Every Platform Behaves Differently

PC, consoles, mobile: each fails differently. None of the built-in reporting gives you the full picture.

#### Players Do the Unexpected

Real players find edge cases no test plan covers. The crash reports that come back are rarely useful.

#### Most Crash Tools Weren't Built for This

Generic crash tools were designed for web and mobile. Native C++, custom engines, and memory dumps need something different.

Crashes happen in every game. Big launch. Small beta. Doesn't matter. What matters is what happens next.

When something breaks, you need the right information fast. What broke? Is it critical or an edge case? How many players are affected? And when you ship the fix, did it hold?

We built BugSplat to answer exactly those questions. We're a small bootstrapped team that's spent nearly 20 years on this problem alongside studios of every size, from developers shipping their first game to teams behind some of the most played titles in the world.

We'd be honored to help with yours. [Try it in your game project](https://app.bugsplat.com/v2/sign-up) for free today.

-The BugSplat Team

###### The fix

## BugSplat was built for game development.

Native crash reporting for game development is what we do. It shows up everywhere: in how crashes get symbolicated, how data gets organized, and how quickly you can go from report to fix.

### Cross-platform crash capture

Console, PC, mobile, custom builds. BugSplat catches crashes silently, no player reports needed. One dashboard, every platform.

### Root-cause grouping & prioritization

Duplicates collapse automatically. You see which crashes hit the most players, on which versions, right now.

### Symbolicated stack traces

Function names and line numbers, not hex dumps. Crashes resolve against the exact build that shipped. Send to Jira, GitHub, or Linear with full context.

### Version-to-version stability monitoring

See what improved, what regressed, and what snuck in after your last release. Know before your players do.

New

### User feedback capture

Not every bug crashes the app. Sometimes the UI just does something wrong, a flow breaks halfway through, or something looks off on a specific device. Those issues used to vanish into Discord threads or get lost in support tickets. Now your QA team and players can report what's broken directly from your game, and it lands in the same dashboard as your crash data with full context attached.

[Learn more](https://www.bugsplat.com/features#user-feedback)

###### Platforms & engines

###### The full picture

## Stability costs less than you think. Ignoring it costs more.

BugSplat fits into every stage of development. Here's where it matters, what it saves you, and what it costs.

When you need it

### Early Development

Catch structural issues before they compound. Stability starts at the prototype.

### Launch

Real-time visibility when players flood in. Focus on the crashes that threaten your release.

### Live Game

Spot regressions early. Keep small issues from turning into support fires.

What it costs without it

### What undetected crashes actually cost

Every day a crash goes undetected, players leave, reviews drop, and support tickets pile up.

estimated cost over

# Growing Teams

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/for/growing-teams

# The bigger your team gets, the more crashes cost you

BugSplat gives growing teams production-grade crash reporting without the operational weight, the unpredictable bill, or the homegrown tool that quietly becomes its own project.

###### Why BugSplat

## Crash reporting that grows with your team

As your team scales, crash data should make every release easier. BugSplat gives growing teams production-grade visibility without the complexity of an observability suite or the maintenance burden of a homegrown tool.

Crashes don't just mean bugs. They mean support emails, context switching, guesswork, and late nights trying to figure out what broke and who it's affecting.

Big platforms can solve this, but they introduce their own operational weight. Homegrown tools work for a while, then quietly become something else to maintain.

BugSplat is production-grade crash reporting that never turns into a project. Stack traces you can read. Grouping that holds up. Data tied to the exact build that shipped. Pricing that doesn't punish you for growing.

You stay focused on shipping. We handle the crash pipeline.

-The BugSplat Team

#### You see crashes before your users tell you

Production crashes land in BugSplat with stack traces, build info, and user context. Your team finds issues before support tickets do.

#### Production-grade crash reporting, zero upkeep

Drop in the SDK and we handle ingestion, grouping, retention, and scale. No homegrown pipeline to babysit on top of the product you're actually building.

#### Focused on crashes, not observability sprawl

Just the crash data your team needs, with onboarding measured in minutes and pricing that doesn't triple the moment you grow.

#### Every release, measured

Crashes are tied to specific builds and versions, so you can see whether the latest release made things better or worse. Stability becomes a metric, not a gut feeling.

## What happens once BugSplat is in place

Crashes stop being mysteries. Your team spends less time investigating and more time shipping.

### You stop hearing about crashes from users first

Wire up each platform once, then desktop, mobile, and web crashes all land in one place. The whole team works from the same data.

### You know which crash to fix first, every morning

Automatic grouping by root cause shows which crashes affect the most users, so you're not guessing where to start.

### The first time you open a report, you understand it

Symbolicated stack traces, logs, and metadata make issues understandable the first time you open them. Send to Jira, GitHub, or Linear with full context.

### You can prove the last release was better than the one before it

See what improved, what regressed, and what snuck in after your last release. Flat monthly pricing means no surprise bills when crash volume spikes.

# Enterprise

Source: https://www.bugsplat.com/for/enterprise

# Enterprise crash reporting without the enterprise runaround

One system for desktop, mobile, web, and consoles. Flat-rate pricing. Security your team can verify. When you reach out, you get the people who built it.

###### Why BugSplat

## Enterprise crash reporting, without the enterprise weight

Large organizations need crash data they can trust, security they can prove, and pricing they can plan around. BugSplat delivers all three, in one tool, without the operational drag of an observability suite.

#### One source of truth across every platform

Desktop, mobile, web, and embedded all report into a single dashboard. QA, engineering, and support work from the same crash data, with no stitching required.

#### Real engineers, not ticket queues

When something goes wrong in production, you talk to people who understand native crash workflows. We help with setup, migrations, symbol pipelines, and the hard stuff after launch.

#### Pricing you can plan around

Flat-rate enterprise contracts with clear limits. A spike in crashes after a release won't double your bill, and procurement gets a number they can defend.

#### The signal, not the noise

Crashes and errors are the most critical thing your users hit. BugSplat surfaces what broke and who it's affecting, instead of burying it in dashboards you have to mine for answers.

When something breaks in production, you don't want a ticket number. You want someone who understands native crash workflows and can actually help.

That's what you get with BugSplat. We help with setup, migrations, and symbol pipelines, and we stick around after you're running.

For larger teams that tends to matter more than people expect. When QA, engineering, and support are all looking at the same crash data, things stop falling through the cracks. Crashes get fixed with less friction and fewer handoffs. That compounds fast across releases.

If that sounds interesting, reach out at [hi@bugsplat.com](mailto:hi@bugsplat.com). We'd like to hear what you're working on.

-The BugSplat Team

## One system. Fewer surprises.

Crash data in five places means five different stories. BugSplat puts it in one, with the security and compliance your organization requires.

### Every crash in one system

Desktop, mobile, web, consoles, and game engines report to the same dashboard. One login. One view of stability across your entire product line.

### Root-cause grouping

Crashes are grouped by root cause and sorted by user impact. Your team sees what matters, not raw volume. Duplicates collapse automatically.

### Shared visibility across teams

QA, engineering, and support see the same crash data. Per-database permissions control who can act on it. Everyone works from the same source of truth.

### Scales with your organization

Project boundaries, volume spikes, and per-database permissions work without adding process or overhead. Add teams and products without rearchitecting.

###### Security & Compliance

## Secure by default

BugSplat is built to meet enterprise security expectations. If you need documentation, we have it. If you have questions, we'll walk you through it.

#### Encryption

Encryption in transit and at rest protects your data throughout its lifecycle.

#### Access Control

SSO, MFA, and per-database user permissions. Decide who can see and act on each project.

#### Infrastructure

Secure infrastructure on AWS with PII scrubbing and data retention controls.

###### Pricing

## Your bill shouldn't spike when your crash volume does

Enterprise plans are contract-based with clear limits. No per-event pricing. No surprise overages. Easy to explain to procurement.

Flat-rate contracts

Fixed monthly cost regardless of crash volume spikes. Budget with confidence.

Custom limits, not tiers

Users, crash volume, and retention tailored to your org. Not shoehorned into a preset plan.

Adjusts through conversation

Need more capacity next quarter? Email us. We'll adjust the contract. No procurement cycle.

## The problems with user-reported bugs

Getting feedback from your users is an incredibly important part of the development and support process. However, traditional methods of learning about your critical defects are often not sufficient for producing great software.

[Read more](https://blog.bugsplat.com/problems-with-user-reported-bugs/)
